subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Kim <alice.kim@finsecure.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the items we promised to follow up on from the discussion about deployment modes and your data isolation requirements: 

1) Summary of what we heard from your team:
- High sensitivity for customer PII and transaction data; must meet strict in-region data residency and strict access controls.
- No customer data may be stored or cached outside your VPC unless explicitly encrypted and controlled.
- Strong requirement for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and audit logs for every inference request.
- Minimal model artifact persistence on shared infrastructure.

2) How Redwood options map to those needs (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to get started but data leaves your network; not a fit if no external egress is allowed.
- Dedicated: isolated GPU pools dedicated to your tenant with guaranteed capacity and network controls; supports customer KMS and audit logs, but data paths may still traverse Redwood-managed control plane.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full customer VPC deployment (or on-prem) where model serving and KV/cache stay inside your network; best fit when you require zero data egress and full KMS/HSM control.

3) Technical clarifications we need from you to confirm fit:
- Confirmation on whether any telemetry/metrics can be sent to Redwood (aggregated only) or must be zero egress.
- Will you require the Redwood control plane to remain accessible (for billing/rollouts) or must that be blocked?
- Expected request volume (QPS and average tokens per request) to size Dedicated pools or Private deployment.

4) Next steps we propose:
- We will share: SOC2 scope doc, our Private deployment architecture diagram, and a short note on caching/kv behavior (attached).
- Please complete the short security questionnaire we’ll attach; that will let our security engineering team validate controls.
- If Private looks required, we’ll arrange a technical POC timeline and SOW draft.

Attaching: SOC2_scope.pdf, redwood-private-arch.png, security-questionnaire-FinSecure.pdf

Dylan (cc) will follow up with a short note on caching behavior and KMS options.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Date: 2026-11-07T17:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We cannot allow any raw customer PII or transaction payloads to leave our VPC. Aggregated telemetry (latency, error rates) may be acceptable if it contains no payloads and is opt-in.
- We require customer-managed KMS keys for encrypting any cached artifacts or model-related files. HSM-backed keys preferred.
- Network: the serving plane must be reachable only via our VPC peering or private link; the control plane can be reachable but must authenticate using mTLS and we need transparent logging of all control-plane operations.
- Regarding caching: we will not accept any long-term shared KV cache that could be reused across tenants. Short-lived request-local caching is fine so long as it is ephemeral and encrypted with our KMS.

Tom (cc) is our platform lead — he’ll share expected QPS and token sizes tomorrow. For now, we are leaning toward Private VPC or on-prem unless you can guarantee no egress and strict KMS control with Dedicated. Can you confirm which features (KMS, audit logs, zero-egress) are available today on Dedicated vs Private?

Thanks,
Alice
Head of Platform, FinSecure
alice.kim@finsecure.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alice Kim <alice.kim@finsecure.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Hi Alice — following up with the technical distinctions and what we can deliver today vs what requires Private deployment/on-prem. Apologies for the longer note; I wanted to be explicit.

What Dedicated provides today:
- Dedicated GPU pools: compute resources reserved only for your tenant; network egress controls at the instance level and IP allow lists.
- Customer KMS support: we support customer-managed keys (KMS) for data-at-rest encryption of persistent artifacts; HSM-backed keys supported via integrations with major cloud KMS providers.
- Audit logs: per-request logs are available and can be exported to your destination (Cloud Storage/S3) via an encrypted pipeline.
- Model cache: models can be pinned per-tenant. There is a short-lived prefix/KV cache used to improve latency; by default some cache metadata is stored within Redwood-managed infra but can be configured to be tenant-isolated for Dedicated.

Limits and caveats for Dedicated:
- Control plane interactions: some orchestration (rollouts/metrics) are mediated by Redwood’s control plane. We support mTLS and customer API keys, but the control plane does see metadata about model versions and routes (no raw payloads).
- Absolute zero-egress: Dedicated cannot guarantee zero egress from the compute plane in every cloud region because of management and autoscaling artifacts—if your policy requires zero possibility of egress (e.g., regulated banking mandates), Private VPC or on-prem is the safe path.

What Private (VPC/on-prem) provides:
- Full isolation: serving runtime lives in your VPC or on-prem and only your network. No outbound egress to Redwood-managed networks unless you enable it.
- KMS/HSM: you supply keys and control; Redwood’s binaries/services use your KMS endpoints.
- Audit & compliance: all logs and telemetry stay in your environment; we provide connectors and a compliance checklist to integrate with your SIEM.
- Deployment models: VPC deployment (managed customer VPC with a private control plane endpoint) or fully air-gapped on-prem with offline bundle.

Recommended next steps for FinSecure:
1) Please confirm whether aggregated telemetry is permitted (yes/no). If yes, which destination (S3/GCS) we should export to.
2) Tom to share QPS and tokens so we can size Dedicated pools and estimate cost for Private.
3) If Private is required, we’ll set up an NDA amendment and schedule a technical POC (2-4 weeks) with our security engineering team.

I’ve attached the Private architecture diagram (redwood-private-arch.png) and the short security questionnaire you can send back. I can also hop on a call with your infra/security team next week to walk the controls.

Best,
